$comment: Registry of reference lexicons the Lexicon lens can benchmark a text against.
Adding one is: drop a CSV beside this file and add an entry here. Nothing in
the package hard-codes a lexicon id, and the UI dropdown is built from this list.
entries_file columns: rank, lemma, gloss, kind (L/F/blank), ref_count, ref_coverage
rank          1-based, dense, ascending by reference-corpus frequency
lemma         NFC, accented, lowercase; a trailing digit marks a homograph
ref_count     occurrences in the reference corpus
ref_coverage  cumulative % of the reference corpus covered through this rank
aliases_file columns: variant, lemma, kind, note — see lexicon.py for how these
are applied. Growing this file is the intended way to fix a match failure.

lexicons.name: Core Greek 5000
lexicons.description: The 5000 most frequent lemmas in a ~469k-token classical and Koine reference corpus, ranked by frequency.

lexicons.name: Greek New Testament
lexicons.description: Every lemma in the Greek New Testament, 5,461 of them, ranked by frequency across 137,554 lemma tokens. Unlike the Core 5000 this list includes proper nouns.
notes: kind is folded from MorphGNT part-of-speech codes: N-/V-/A-/D-/I- lexical, RA/C-/P-/RP/RD/RR/RI/X- function.
Glosses are BORROWED from greek-core-5k where the two lists name the same word (51% of entries);
the GNT data carries no definitions of its own, and the rest are blank rather than invented.
MorphGNT cites movable consonants in parentheses (`ουτω(ς)`); the entry takes the fuller
spelling and the bare one is an alias, since the parenthesised form matches no real text.
